explanation: Faithful negative resolution. It asserts that not all A, B with √n = O(A(n)) and √n = O(B(n)) admit infinitely many solutions to a₁ + b₂ = a₂ + b₁ with a₁ ≠ a₂, i.e. a₁ − a₂ = b₁ − b₂ ≠ 0. Ruzsa's even-bit/odd-bit sets give unique representations n = a + b, so there are no nontrivial solutions. Nat.count counts [0, n), which is asymptotically the same as |A ∩ [1, N]|. Linked formal proof by van Doorn.
